questions.q: What does AWS CloudTrail primarily track, compared to CloudWatch and X-Ray?
options: Application performance metrics only
Every API call made against the AWS account, by any user or service
Distributed traces across microservices
Database query performance
questions.explain: Unlike CloudWatch (metrics/logs) and X-Ray (application traces), CloudTrail is an account-level audit log of API activity — who did what, when, and from where.

questions.q: How long does CloudTrail's Event history retain management events by default, with no configuration?
options: 7 days
30 days
90 days
Indefinitely
questions.explain: Event history is enabled automatically for every AWS account and retains 90 days of management events with zero setup required.

questions.q: What is the difference between a management event and a data event in CloudTrail?
options: Management events are control-plane actions (create/modify/delete resources); data events are higher-volume operations on the resources themselves and are off by default
They are identical; the names are just historical
Data events are control-plane actions; management events are data-plane operations
Management events never get logged at all
questions.explain: Management events cover things like launching an instance or changing an IAM policy. Data events (like S3 GetObject) are data-plane operations, much higher volume, and must be explicitly enabled.

questions.q: Why would a team set up a CloudTrail trail instead of relying only on Event history?
options: Trails are required to view any CloudTrail data at all
To retain events beyond 90 days and deliver them continuously to S3 across all regions
Trails are a faster way to launch EC2 instances
Event history cannot be filtered by event name
questions.explain: Event history is convenient but temporary (90 days) and regional. A trail continuously delivers events to S3 (and optionally CloudWatch Logs) for longer retention and multi-region coverage.

options: Automatically deletes old trails to save storage
Analyzes management event patterns and flags statistically unusual activity automatically
Converts CloudTrail logs into CloudWatch metrics only
Blocks suspicious API calls in real time
questions.explain: CloudTrail Insights detects unusual patterns in management event activity, such as a sudden spike in RunInstances calls, without anyone having to write a detection rule in advance.
